title: Certify deficiency-zero hypotheses for small reaction networks
statement: For a finite supplied network of mass-action reactions, compute delta = number_of_complexes - number_of_linkage_classes - rank(stoichiometric_matrix), test weak reversibility, and issue a traceable applicability certificate for the deficiency-zero theorem. Begin with at most four species, six complexes and ten reactions; these limits are curator chosen.
source_locator: ACK Definitions 2.1-2.4 and Theorem 3.1; Baez theorem
status_basis: The theorem and hypotheses are verified in the opened sources. The finite input limits and certificate task are curator-designed calibration work.
plain_summary: Turn a reaction diagram into a checkable explanation of whether a known structural theorem applies. This links chemistry and biology to graph algorithms and exact linear algebra without treating a model as an observed mechanism.
assumptions: Finite set of species and distinct nonnegative-integer stoichiometric complexes.
Deterministic, autonomous mass-action kinetics with strictly positive fixed rate constants.
The theorem applies on positive stoichiometric compatibility classes; stability is relative to the class.
Duplicate reactions and self-loops must have an explicitly documented normalization convention.
scope: Curator-chosen inputs up to four species, six complexes and ten directed reactions. Include A+B <-> C and C <-> D as one fully specified example network, with positive rate symbols; this fixture is proposed and has not been run.
target: An exact structural certificate with the theorem's supported conclusion, or a precise report of failed hypotheses.
success_criteria: Produce a canonical complex list, incidence data, stoichiometric matrix and exact rank certificate.
Produce connected-component and directed-return-path certificates for linkage count and weak reversibility.
Compute deficiency exactly and state the theorem only when all hypotheses apply.
If a hypothesis fails, report inapplicability rather than infer instability or nonexistence.
Separate structural certification from identifying whether the network represents a real chemical or biological system.
known_results: ACK Theorem 3.1 states uniqueness of the equilibrium in each positive compatibility class and local asymptotic stability relative to that class for weakly reversible deficiency-zero mass-action networks.
Baez gives a complementary existence proof through linear algebra. Feinberg's directory records historical sources and corrections.
prerequisites: Directed graphs and strongly connected components.
Exact rank, conservation laws and stoichiometric subspaces.
Mass-action ODEs, complex balance and relative local stability.
significance: Provides a reusable hypothesis-checking baseline for model sciences. It can prevent invalid theorem transfers and supports later comparisons of reaction-network structures.

relations.explanation: A structural certificate can establish the hypotheses used to obtain a complex-balanced deterministic equilibrium before the stochastic product-form task.
Structural perturbation studies need reliable recomputation of graph and rank invariants.

requirements.experiment: None for the graph-and-theorem certificate. Validating rates, well-mixing and the proposed mechanism requires separate data or experiments.
requirements.data: A complete reaction list with species ordering and kinetic convention. No new empirical data for this calibration.
requirements.compute: Small exact integer matrices and graph traversals under the declared input bounds. Local laptop-class work is an untested planning assumption; larger symbolic equilibrium computations are outside scope.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Mass action, positive rates and positive compatibility classes. Does not transfer automatically to delays, spatial PDEs, stochastic dynamics, non-mass-action kinetics or time-varying forcing.

ai_assessment.rationale: The structural part is well suited to generated code and exact certificates, but a reviewer must first approve representation conventions and the limited theorem conclusion.

clarity.reason: Finite input and the applicable theorem are explicit.

decomposability.reason: Parsing, graph structure, rank and theorem matching are separable.

methods.reason: Author resources and a primary paper state the required concepts.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Exact linear algebra and graph algorithms apply directly.

checkability.reason: Certificates can be independently recomputed at the proposed small sizes.

expertise.reason: A CRNT reviewer must distinguish complex balance and detailed balance and assess kinetic assumptions.

significance.reason: Reusable verification baseline; no new reaction-network theorem is claimed.

verification_difficulty.reason: Structural checks are modest; scope errors in stability claims are more subtle.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No AI or implementation has been tested. Small input bounds are chosen for inspectability and do not estimate success rates.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI with literature retrieval, exact algebra or rational linear algebra, code generation, and access to a human domain reviewer.

obstacles: Treating species as complexes or counting duplicate complexes twice.
Confusing reversibility, weak reversibility, detailed balance and complex balance.
Changing local stability into a global-attraction claim.
Assuming that theorem inapplicability implies a negative dynamical result.

steps: Review the input reaction semantics and deduplication convention.
Compare complex and species matrices with the supplied diagram.
Check exact rank and graph witnesses independently.
Verify each hypothesis against the cited theorem and retain its positivity and relative-stability clauses.
Review any biological or chemical interpretation separately.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Moderate for a CRNT specialist; a graph or linear-algebra reviewer can check only the structural layer.
validation.statement_alignment: The certificate establishes theorem applicability, not global attraction, empirical adequacy, or a complete classification of all possible dynamics.

known_attempts: Existing theorem and proofs are documented by Horn, Jackson, Feinberg, Baez and ACK. No project implementation or model trial exists.
unresolved_checks: Approve the small input format and example network before execution.
Check the version of any theorem used for an expanded global-convergence claim; this card deliberately makes no such claim.
The empirical validity of any future supplied network requires independent review.

Historical references and author credit: Feinberg, Chemical Reaction Network Theory (Ohio State); Baez (2012), Network Theory Part 24.
attribution.curator_credit: Compiled for Theory Research Atlas with AI assistance.

status_search.result: The full theorem statement, structural definitions and author bibliography were opened and compared. It is an established-result calibration.
status_search.limitations: No implementation or mathematical experiment was executed. Original 1972 articles were credited through the author directory, not claimed as fully read.

epistemic_layers.formal_validity: Conditional structural theorem application can be certified under mass-action assumptions.
epistemic_layers.empirical_support: Real chemistry and cell biology may violate ideal mixing, closure, rate and scale assumptions; this task supplies no empirical confirmation.

correctness.basis: The cited literature supports the problem statement. No project answer has been submitted for review.

novelty.basis: The target is a known result; no originality is claimed for the selected scope. Any later novelty claim requires a literature check.
